questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which ion helps in opening and closing of stomata?
questions.solution: According to active <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> theory of Levitt, opening of stomata occurs due to influx of <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> into guard cells. The source of <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions are nearby subsidiary and epidermal cells. The stomatal closure is considered to be brought about by exertion of <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math>from the guard cells to epidermal tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The adsorption of water by hydrophilic compounds like cellulose and pectin in root hair cell wall is called _______.
questions.solution:
It is a physical process which involves adsorption and/or absorption of water by hydrophilic substances without forming a solution e.g., wooden doors absorb water and swell up in rainy season and seeds of pea and gram when placed in water swell up due to imbibition

The imbibition process involves diffusion and capillary action.
In imbibition, Liquid substance (water) is called imbibate, and solid colloidal substance is called imbibant. e.g. the gum, dry wood, cell protoplasm, seed coat, etc. Due to imbibition, water molecules remain held (absorbed) over the surface of hydrophilic particles and also remain held between the space of particles of imbibant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is true?
options: The positive hydrostatic pressure is called turgor pressure.
Diffusion pressure deficit equals osmotic pressure of a solution plus wall pressure.
Diffusion is more rapid in liquids than in gases.
Diffusion of water through a semi-permeable membrane is called imbibition.
questions.solution: Turgor pressure is exerted by the fluid inside the cell on the cell wall. It pushes the plasma membrane against the cell wall due to the osmotic flow of water through the permeable membrane. As it acts inside the cell to outside it is positive hydrostatic pressure, which is opposed by equal and opposite wall pressure (negative pressure). Diffusion is the movement of particles of gases, liquids, and solids from a region of higher free energy to a region of lower free energy. It is more rapid in gases, as compared to liquids as the density of gases is lower than that of liquids. Imbibition is the absorption of water by solid particles of an adsorbent substance without forming a solution.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In rainy season, door gets swelled due to
questions.solution: In rainy season, door gets swelled due to the phenomenon of imbibition. It is the process of absorption of water without forming a solution.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Active transport of ions by the cell requires
questions.solution: During active transport of ions, the energy is usually provided in the form of by ATP or by the concentration gradient of ions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Carbohydrates are commonly found as starch in plant storage organs. Which of the following five properties of starch (a-e) make it useful as a storage material?

(a) Easily translocated.
(b) Chemically non-reactive.
(c) Easily digested by animals.
(d) Osmotically inactive.
(e) Synthesized during photosynthesis.

The useful properties are
questions.solution: Starch is a plant storage polysaccharide. It is chemically non-reactive and osmotically inactive polysaccharides of much greater molecular weight. Carbohydrates perform a vital role in living organisms. Starch and other polysaccharides serve as energy storage in plants, particularly in seeds, tubers, etc. which provide a major energy source for animals, including humans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The force of tension cohesion exceeds root pressure on a
questions.solution: It is so because the transpiration rate is very high on a sunny day.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The rate of transpiration increases with the decrease of
questions.solution: With the decrease in atmospheric pressure, the vapour pressure gradient across the stomata increases, and this causes rapid flow of vapours to the atmosphere. So with the decrease in atmospheric pressure rate of transpiration increases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic bridges between adjacent plant cells, lined by
questions.solution: Plasmodesmata are plasma membrane‐lined pores that span the adjoining walls of plant cells. The symplast pathway is where water moves from cell to cell in the cytoplasm via the plasma membranes and plasmodesmata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following does not play any role in the movement of water through the xylem?
options: <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>/ATPase pump at the xylem element membrane
questions.solution: ATPase pumps are found on the membranes of the living component i.e. cell or organelle. Because xylem is a dead tissue through which conduction of water occurs, therefor no ATPase action is found in the xylem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The water potential and osmotic potential of pure water is
questions.solution: Osmotic potential is the potential of a solution to cause water movement into it across a semipermeable membrane. Water potential is the tendency of water to leave a system, which is zero for pure water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most widely accepted theory of ascent of sap in trees is
questions.solution: Transpiration pull and cohesion theory was put forward by Dixon and Jolly in 1894. According to this theory, the water rises due to the transpiration pull, continuity of the water column, and the cohesive power of water molecules from the lower part of the roots to the higher peaks of the trees.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Root pressure is maximum when
options: Transpiration is high and absorption is very low
Transpiration is very low and absorption is high
Transpiration and absorption both are high
Transpiration and absorption both are low.
questions.solution: Root pressure is the pressure that develops in tracheary elements of xylem due to the accumulation of water. It occurs due to active absorption of water and is maximum when the rate of absorption is high and the rate of transpiration is low.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following has the maximum water potential?
questions.solution: Water potential is the difference in free energy or chemical potential per unit molal volume of water in a system and that of pure water at the same temperature and pressure. The water potential of pure water is zero and it decreases on the addition of solutes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell increases in volume, if the external medium is
questions.solution: If the plasmolysed cell (flaccid cell) is placed in a hypotonic solution then endosmosis occurs, which makes the cell again turgid (volume increases).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The movement of mineral ions into plant root cells as a result of diffusion is called
questions.solution: A simple process of diffusion aids in the absorption of the mineral salts during its high concentration in the soil/outer solution than in the cell sap of the root cells. Diffusion is a passive absorption because the movement of mineral ions into plant root cells takes place without energy utilization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Path of water movement from soil to exarch xylem is
questions.solution:
The path of water movement from soil to xylem is:

soil→root hair→cortex→endodermis→pericycle→protoxylem→metaxylem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the main function of anti-transpirants?
options: Reduce the rate of transpiration without affecting carbon assimilation
Reduce the rate of transpiration affecting carbon assimilation
Reduce the rate of transpiration affecting growth of plants
Reduce the rate of transpiration affecting protein synthesis of plant
questions.solution: Anti-transpirants reduce the rate of transpiration without affecting the metabolic process i.e., transpirants are permeable to CO2 and O2 to allow photosynthesis and respiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main function of phloem is translocation of
questions.solution: Phloem is the chief food conducting tissue of vascular plants responsible for translocation of organic solutes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following is/are pre-requisite(s) for imbibition?

(a) Presence of mucilage in the adsorbent.
(b) The affinity between the adsorbent and the liquid.
(c) Water potential gradient between the adsorbent and the liquid.
(d) Presence of cuticle on the surface of the adsorbent.

Choose the correct option from the following.
questions.solution:
Absorption of fluid by a colloid or porous solid that often results in swelling is known as imbibitions. Two conditions are prerequisites for imbibition, i.e.,
a) a water potential gradient must exist between the surface of the absorbent and the liquid imbibed, and
b) an affinity must exist between the component of the absorbent and the imbibed substance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A leaf peeling of Tradescantia is kept in a medium having 10% NaCl. After a few minutes, if we observe the leaf peel under the microscope, we are likely to see
options: Entry of water into the cell
Diffusion of NaCl into the cell
Exit of water from the cell
questions.solution: When a cell is placed in a hypertonic solution then exosmosis occurs. Due to exosmosis, the protoplasm shrinks and leaves the cell wall and thus becomes flaccid, which is called plasmolysis. Thus, exosmosis leads to plasmolysis. Since 10% NaCl solution is a hypertonic solution as compared to cell sap exosmosis, i.e., movement of water from inside to outside the cell will occur.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lowering in magnitude of water potential due to dissolution of a solute is called
questions.solution: On addition of solute free energy of water molecules decreases and this decrease in free energy depends on the concentration of solute present and know as solute potential or osmotic potential.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What will be the effect of the accumulation of <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions in guard cells?
questions.solution:
When the amount of solutes increases, osmotic potential decreases, and total water potential decreases.

Opening and closure of the stomatal pore are mediated by changes in the turgor pressure of the two guard cells. The turgor pressure of guard cells is controlled by movements of large quantities of ions and sugars into and out of it. Guard cells have cell walls of varying thickness and differently oriented cellulose microfibers, causing them to bend outward when they are turgid, which in turn, causes stomata to open.

Stomata open when there is an osmotic gain of water, occurring from the inflow of K+ ions from neighboring cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell swells up when kept in
questions.solution: A cell swells up when kept in a hypotonic solution due to the process of endosmosis. Endosmosis is the movement of water into the cell and such a plant cell is referred to as turgid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water potential is equal to
questions.solution: Water potential is defined as the difference between the chemical potential of water at any point in a system and that of pure water under standard conditions. The unit of measurement of water potential is the pascal, Pa (1 megapascal, Mpa = 10 bars). It is represented by greek letter PSi (ψ). Water potential has two components solute potential which is always negative and pressure potential which is usually positive. Therefore, water potential ψ<sub>w</sub> is expressed as ψ<sub>w</sub> = ψ<sub>s</sub> + ψ<sub>p.</sub>

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following:

i. For a solution at atmospheric pressure Ψw = Ψs
ii. Ψw  (water potential) of a cell is affected by solute potential only
iii. Ψp  (pressure potential) is usually positive in xylem during the day

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Water potential of a solution is the sum total of four components: gravitational potential, osmotic(solute) potential, matric potential and pressure potential. But, since matric potential and gravitational potential are negligible, water potential is generally more affected by solute and pressure potential. Pressure potential of water during the standard stage is 0 MPa. The positive value of water potential within the cell is referred to as turgor pressure. During the day when transpiration is high, pressure potential of the xylem mostly is negative since water is evaporated and its turgor pressure is less.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the type of transport labelled (i), (ii), and (iii) in the diagram given below.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water potential of actively absorbing cells is
questions.solution: Water potential is regarded as the tendency of water to leave a system. Pure water has the highest possible water potential which is zero. All solutions have water potential lower than that of pure water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The mechanism universally accepted to describe the translocation of sugars from source to sink is called
options: Translocation of food due to TP gradient and imbibition force
Translocation of food due to turgor pressure (TP) gradient
Translocation of food due to imbibition force
questions.solution: Munch hypothesis is based on translocation of food due to turgor pressure (TP) gradient.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Different substances move independently along their concentration gradient in mass flow.
Active absorption of ions from the soil by the root is mainly affected by respiratory activity of root.
The translocation of organic solutes in sieve tube members is supported by mass flow.
Root pressure develops due to active absorption.
questions.solution: Mass or bulk flow is the movement of substances in bulk from source to sink as a result of pressure differences. Mass flow is not to be confused with diffusion which depends on concentration gradients within a medium rather than pressure gradients of the medium itself.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Translocation of food in plants was demonstrated by
questions.solution: A simple experiment, called girdling, was used to identify the tissues through which food is transported. On the trunk of a tree, a ring of bark up to a depth of the phloem layer can be carefully removed. In the absence of a downward movement of food, the portion of the bark above the ring on the stem becomes swollen after a few weeks. This simple experiment shows that phloem is the tissue responsible for translocation of food; and that transport takes place in one direction, i.e., towards the roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Stomata are not found in
questions.solution: Hydrophytes that are fully submerged in water have no stomata or waxy cuticle as these are not required because these plants live in water. Since algae are primarily aquatic in nature and there is no threat of overheating of body therefore they do not have stomata at their surface.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In plants, <u>                         </u> potential in the water column in the xylem plays a major role in water transport up a stem.
questions.solution: Pressure potential is usually positive, though in plants negative potential or tension in the water column in the xylem plays a major role in water transport up a stem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The continuous upward flow of water stream in tall trees is maintained due to ______________________.
options: Cohesive force between water molecules only
Cohesive force between water molecules and transpiration pull
questions.solution: The continuous upward flow of water stream in a tall tree is maintained due to cohesive force between water molecules and transpiration pull.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Transpiration has more than one purpose. Which of the following is not the purpose of transpiration?
options: Creates transpiration pull for absorption and transport in plants.
Cools leaf surfaces by evaporative cooling.
Transports minerals from the soil to all parts of the plant.
Gives high tensile strength to water column present in xylem.
questions.solution: Transpiration creates a transpiration pull which causes ascent of sap. The cohesive and adhesive properties of water molecules forms the unbroken continuous water column in the xylem. The water molecules are held together by strong cohesion force due to hydrogen bonds and the force of adhesion which holds water to the walls of xylem vessels. The surface tension accounts for high capillarity through tracheids and vessels.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Look at the following diagram showing facilitated diffusion across the membrane. Identify its type.
questions.solution: The two molecules A and B move in the opposite direction in the given figure; hence, the diffusion is antiport.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following statements are not correct?

[I] In a flowering plant the substances that would need to be transported are water, mineral nutrients, organic nutrients and plant growth regulators.
[II] Over small distances, substances move by diffusion and by cytoplasmic streaming supplemented only by passive transport.
[III] Organic and mineral nutrients undergo multidirectional transport through the xylem.
[IV] From the storage organs, organic compounds are later re-exported.
[V] Phytohormones and other chemical signals are transported to maintain and regulate the plant functions.
questions.solution: Statement II and III are wrong. The flow of substances in the xylem is unidirectional and cytoplasmic streaming is caused by a regular change in the structure of cytoskeleton which is an energy-consuming process. Cytoplasmic streaming, also called protoplasmic streaming and cyclosis, is where there is flow inside the cytoplasm. It is typically observed in large plant and animal cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Water potential is the chemical potential of the water
Pressure potential is zero in a flaccid cell
Water potential equals solute potential in a fully turgid cell
questions.solution:
Water potential is the difference in the free energy or chemical potential per unit molal volume of water in a system and that of pure water at the same temperature and pressure. It is represented by greek letter Ψ (psi) or more accurately Ψw

Water potential or Ψw is the sum total of Ψs and Ψp.

Ψw = Ψs + Ψp

where Ψs→ solute potential

Ψp→ pressure potential

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The osmotic pressure of 1 M solution of sucrose is 22.4 atm. What will be the osmotic potential of 0.1 M sucrose solution?
questions.solution:
Osmotic potential is a modern term for osmotic pressure. The osmotic pressure for a solution is positive, but its value is negative for osmotic potential.

Hence, Osmotic pressure = - Osmotic potential.

The osmotic pressure of 1M solution is 22.4 atm, hence for a 0.1M solution it will be 2.24 atm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phenomenon of uptake of water at the expense of energy by the cell and usually against the osmotic gradient is known as
questions.solution: In active absorption, uptake of substance occurs against the concentration gradient by using energy in the form of ATP. When absorption of substances occurs along the concentration gradient than energy is not consumed and this is called passive absorption.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not common between facilitated transport and active transport?
questions.solution:
Property Facilitated transport Active transport
Requires special membrane proteins Yes Yes
Highly selective Yes Yes
Transport saturates Yes Yes
Uphill transport No Yes
Requires ATP energy No Yes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: For a solution at atmospheric pressure, water potential is
questions.solution: <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi></mrow></msub></math> is the water potential of cell, and it the kinetic energy present in water molecules. If some solutes is dissolved in pure water, the solution has fewer free water and the concentration of water decreases, reducing its water potential. For a solution at atmospheric pressure, <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi></mrow></msub></math> is equal to concentration of solutes present in it or <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msub></math> .

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The suction pressure of the cell is
questions.solution:
The negative pressure difference formed between two points that enables flow of gas or liquid to a lower state from higher state is called suction pressure.

The pressure that enables entry of water into the cell due to osmosis is the osmotic pressure (OP) and it is considered negative. The pressure developed in cell due to entry of water and acting opposite to the OP is called turgor pressure (TP). It is a negative pressure as it resists entry of water in cell. The difference between these two results in diffusion pressure deficit (DPD) that equates to the suction pressure. It is directly proportional to the height of the plant/tree.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect w.r.t cytoplasmic streaming.
options: Symplastic movement may be aided by cytoplasmic streaming.
Cytoplasmic streaming can be observed in cells of the Hydrilla leaf.
Over long distances, substances move by cytoplasmic streaming supplemented by passive transport.
questions.solution: Over small distances, substances move by diffusion and by cytoplasmic streaming supplemented by active transport.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Root pressure is maximum when
options: transpiration is high and absorption is low.
transpiration is very low and absorption is high.
questions.solution: The positive pressure in the plants responsible for pushing up water in the stem is known as root pressure. The root pressure is observed maximum in the night or early morning when the evaporation is low and the water absorption is high due to excessive collection of water. Root pressure provides a push in the overall process of water transportation in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Exudation and guttation are due to
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure developed in the cells of roots in the root system is termed as root pressure and this supports in the rise of the cell sap towards the leaves. Root pressure results in exudation and as well as guttation.

Fluid emitted via the roots of the plants are referred to as exudates and the process is called as exudation.

Loss of impure water from plant, generally from the margins of leaves is termed as guttation. The water contains a dilute solution of different organic and inorganic substances. Guttation occurs due to low rate of transpiration and more water absorption. This higher rate of absorption develops root pressure and pushes the excess water out of the specialized pores of veins called hydathodes. Guttation is a type of exudation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Diffusion rates are affected by:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: The rate of diffusion is affected by the concentration gradient, membrane permeability, temperature, and pressure. Diffusion takes place as long as there is a difference between the concentrations of a substance across a barrier. However, diffusion stops, when the concentrations of the substance on either side of the barrier become equal.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: DPD =
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>
questions.solution: The pressure that is exerted by the movement of molecules from the region of higher concentration to the region of lower concentration is known as diffusion pressure. The DPD term was coined by B.S.Meyer in 1938. The reduction in diffusion pressure of the solvent in a system over its pure state is called diffusion pressure deficit. It can be calculated through this formula i.e. OP-WP. Here OP is the osmotic pressure. It is that minimum pressure which is required to stop the inward movement of water through the semipermeable membrane. WP is wall pressure that is exerted by the wall to the protoplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following determines the diffusion of water from one cell to another?
questions.solution: The diffusion of water from one cell to another is a passive process that doesn't require any ATP.DPD is a diffusion pressure deficit and it was described as suction pressure by Renner in 1915. The DPD is the amount by which the diffusion pressure of water solvent in a solution is lower than that of pure solvent or water and they oppose the diffusion. Water movement occurs from lower DPD to higher DPD.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statement is incorrect regarding diffusion pressure deficit (DPD)?
options: DPD is directly proportional to the solute concentration of the system.
DPD of fully turgid cell becomes zero
DPD for a plasmolysed cell is highest
DPD of flaccid cell is always more than osmotic pressure.
questions.solution: DPD is the difference in diffusion pressure of a solution to its pure solvent. On addition of solute DPD increases. DPD = OP – TP. For a flaccid cell TP is zero thus DPD is equal to OP. For a plasmolysed cell TP is negative thus DPD is maximum and is equal to OP + TP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following transport mechanisms shows saturation of transport but does not show uphill transport?
questions.solution: Facillitated diffusion is helped diffusion of molecules from the region of their higher concentration to their lower concentration, with the help of trans membrane or channel proteins. Since carrier proteins are involved it shows saturation of transport when all carrier proteins are involved in the movement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The absorbed water can rise to the highest point by
questions.solution: The transpirational pull is responsible for the transport of water to the highest point, from the roots to the leaves of the tree. This transpirational pull is due to the cohesion of water molecules (attraction between similar molecules), this force maintains a continuous channel for water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cohesive force of water is due to
questions.solution: Cohesion refers to attraction between molecules of same kind. Cohesive force is found in water molecule due to ability of hydrogen bonding. It is a special type of dipole-dipole interaction between molecules. In water hydrogen bond is a dynamic attraction between neighboring water molecules which involves one hydrogen atom located between the two oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Most herbaceous plants have only about ____________ of its fresh weight as dry matter.
questions.solution: Water is essential for all physiological activities of the plant and plays a very important role in all living organisms. It provides the medium in which most substances are dissolved. The protoplasm of the cells is nothing but water in which different molecules are dissolved and (several particles) suspended. A watermelon has over 92 per cent water; most herbaceous plants have only about 10 to 15 per cent of its fresh weight as dry matter. Of course, distribution of water within a plant varies – woody parts have relatively very little water, while soft parts mostly contain water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell A with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> is surrounded by the cells with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> , what will be the direction of water movement?
questions.solution:
DPD is a diffusion pressure deficit and it is used to find out the direction of movement of water. The movement of water will take place from low DPD to high DPD and it can be calculated through given formula i.e.

DPD= Osmotic pressure-Turgor pressure
 
Cell A Cell B
OP=6 OP=3
TP=WP=5 TP=WP=2
So DPD=6-5=1 DPD=3-2=1

The DPD of both the cells is coming equal. So there will be no movement of water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Accumulation of which one of the following acids results in the closure of stomata.
questions.solution: According to <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> pump theory during the closure of stomata, ABA stops the energy dependant proton pump in guard cell, thus <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> diffuses out of the cell and <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> enters inside, which combines with malate ion to form malic acid. OP of guard cells decreases thus stomata close.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In flowering plants, the substances that would need to be transported are:
questions.solution: In a flowering plant, the substances that would need to be transported are water, mineral nutrients, organic nutrients and plant growth regulators.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When a solute is mixed, the water potential of the cell
questions.solution: Water molecules possess kinetic energy. In liquid and gaseous form they are in random motion that is both rapid and constant. The greater the concentration of water in a system, the greater is its kinetic energy or water potential. If some solute is dissolved in pure water, the solution has fewer free water and the concentration of water decreases, reducing its water potential.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process by which substances are transported over a long distance in plants through the vascular system is called:
questions.solution: Over small distances substances move by diffusion and by cytoplasmic streaming supplemented by active transport .transport over longer distances proceeds through the vascular system (the xylem and phloem) is called translocation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Organic compounds synthesis in the plant is transported in which of the following ways in flowering plants:
options: From leaves to other part and storage organ
Re exported from storage organ to other part
questions.solution: Compounds synthesised in the photosynthetic leaves are exported to all other parts of the plant including storage organs. From the storage organ they are later re-exported.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If the cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, what will happen?
questions.solution: Osmosis is the process which takes place due to difference in the concentration of solutions. The movement of molecules always takes place from a solution of less concentration to a solution of high concentration. Hypertonic solution is one which has a higher concentration of solute as compared to the other solution, therefore if a cell is placed in a hypertonic solution it will lose water due to exosmosis ( transfer of molecules outside the cell) and become a plasmolysed cell(shrinking of the cell).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In facilitated diffusion
options: the hydrolysis of ATP is required to facilitate diffusion.
specific substances are transported against their concentration gradient.
membrane phospholipids create a channel that permits diffusion of a specific substance.
a membrane protein binds to a specific solute and then undergoes a conformational change.
questions.solution: Facilitated diffusion is a kind of diffusion wherein there is passive transport(cannot transport via self) of molecules spontaneously across a biological membrane with the help of the protein molecules of the membrane which act as the carriers for the polar molecules in this diffusion process. In this process, the membrane carrier proteins get bounded to the specific solute to be transported and undergo a series of conformational changes (macromolecular shape change) to transfer the solute across the membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water will be absorbed by root hairs when:
options: the concentration of salts in soil is high
the concentration of solutes in the cell sap is high
they are separated from soil by a semipermeable membrane
questions.solution: The movement of molecules always takes place from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. The soil has a higher concentration of water as compared to the water in the root hair, this allows the water from the soil to move to the root hair by facilitated diffusion. This process of diffusion and absorption is possible only when the cell sap (the watery fluid in the plant vacuole) has a lower concentration of water and a higher concentration of solute as compared to the root hair so that the root hair absorbs the water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process by which hydrophilic molecule move across the membrane by proteins is known as
questions.solution: The membrane proteins do not set up a concentration gradient; a concentration gradient must already be present for a molecule to diffuse even if facilitated by the proteins. This process is called facilitated diffusion

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Diffusion of a molecule from low concentration to the high concentration
options: take place in presence of proteins
questions.solution: Diffusion cannot cause net transport of molecule from a low to a high concentration-this would require input of energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is reducing and non-reactive sugar?
questions.solution: A sugar without a hemiacetal is non-reducing because it does not behave as a reducing agent toward oxidizing metal salts. Sucrose is one example of a non-reducing sugar. Different tests can work out whether sugar is reducing or non-reducing, by detecting the presence of free aldehyde or ketone groups. Sucrose is less reactive and more likely to survive the journey in the phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Girdle experiment involves the removal of ring wood of tissue outside the vascular cambium from the tree trunk. This leads to death of plant because
options: food does not travel down and the root becomes starved.
questions.solution: A simple experiment, called girdling, was used to identify the tissues through which food is transported. On the trunk of a tree, a ring of bark up to a depth of the phloem layer can be carefully removed. This simple experiment shows that phloem is the tissue responsible for translocation of food and that transport takes place in one direction, i.e., towards the roots. Vascular cambium forms phloem tissue outside and xylem towards the inside. Food synthesised in the leaves move to different parts of the plant through the phloem. When we remove this outer part (phloem), the lower parts do not get food and eventually die.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The function of nucleated cells in phloem is to _____
options: provide energy to sieve elements for active transport.
load sucrose into sieve elements by passive transport.
load sucrose into sieve elements by active transport.
questions.solution: Companion cells move sugar and amino acids in and out of the sieve elements. In "source" tissue such as leaf, companion cells use transmembrane proteins to take up sugar and amino acids by active transport. Movement of sugars in the phloem begins at the source, where sugars are loaded (actively transported) into a sieve tube. Loading sets up a water potential gradient that facilitates the movement of sugar.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following properties is observed in the case of facilitated transport?

a) highly selective
b) transport saturates
c) uphill transport
d) requires special membrane proteins
e) requires ATP energy
questions.solution: In facilitated diffusion special proteins help move substances across membranes without expenditure of ATP energy. Facilitated diffusion cannot cause net transport of molecules from a low to a high concentration – this would require input of energy. Transport rate reaches a maximum when all of the protein transporters are being used (saturation). Facilitated diffusion is very specific: it allows cell to select substances for uptake. It is sensitive to inhibitors which react with protein side chains.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ascent of xylem sap, caused due to transpiration, depends mainly on three physical properties of water. These properties result in
options: low tensile strength but high capillarity.
low tensile strength as well as low capillarity.
high tensile strength as well as high capillarity.
high tensile strength but low capillarity.
questions.solution:
The transpiration driven ascent of xylem sap depends mainly on the following physical properties of water:
• Cohesion – mutual attraction between water molecules.
• Adhesion – the attraction of water molecules to polar surfaces (such as the surface of tracheary elements).
• Surface Tension – water molecules are attracted to each other in the liquid phase more than to water in the gas phase.
These properties give water high tensile strength, i.e., an ability to resist a pulling force, and high capillarity, i.e., the ability to rise in thin tubes. In plants, capillarity is aided by the small diameter of the tracheary elements – the tracheids and vessel elements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for the maintenance of turgidity of a plant cell?
questions.solution: Vacuoles are large organelles found in plant cells. Vacuoles have a membrane, tonoplast that surrounds it. This organelle help plant cell with storage of plant products and also water. Since it can store water, it provides structural support to the cell and also regulates the osmotic expansion and contraction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Wilting occurs in plants irrigated in soil having excessive salts due to
questions.solution: Excessive use of fertilizers causes exosmosis as the outer medium will become hypertonic. In such a condition, osmotic withdrawal of water from all parts of plant takes place. This kind of loss of water causes wilting in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Solute potential of pure water and its solution are:
questions.solution: By definition," Water potential is the potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water in reference conditions." Thus, water will move from a higher water potential region to the lower potential region through the semipermeable membrane. It can be summarized as total of pressure potential, gravity potential and solute potential. Water potential of a fluid is reduced due to presence of solute as water molecules cluster around solute particles and this is referred to as solute potential. Pure water has the water potential of zero as there is no solute present and the pressure in the system is zero. Since, presence of solute particles reduces the water potential, thus, water potential of a solution will be less water potential of pure water that is less than 0.
